title: Regression playground and A/B simulator — SummitTech lab walkthrough
summary: Introductory demo of Redwood's evaluation and quality-monitoring features focused on prompt sets, regression alerts, and A/B comparison simulation. Team discussed hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs, request for benchmark run, and agreed next steps for a short pilot and technical deep-dive to validate latency/cost for SummitTech's customer-facing summarization API.
topics: Regression alerting thresholds and signal types
Hosted vs Dedicated routing and cost/latency tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Start: 09:31 PT
Duration: 58m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Aisha, Ben, Clara (SummitTech)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, um this is Jordan from Redwood Inference, i'm the account lead, joining with Priya who's gonna run through the console and the evaluation sandbox, uh quick hellos?
[00:08] Aisha: hi yeah thanks, appreciate you making time, we've got about an hour, want to see how you guys do prompt regression and the a slash b simulation, and also need to understand cost impact for our summarization endpoint.
[00:16] Priya: great, i'll start with a short overview then jump into the demo environment, fair?
[00:20] Ben: sounds good, we have a few infra constraints — region eu-west-1 preferred and we need vpc isolation for some customers.
[00:28] Jordan: noted, we'll call out hosted+dedicated routing options. quick qual — how big is your traffic and what p95 latency target?
[00:36] Clara: around 60 req/s peak, p95 target ~800ms for the short summaries, cost is also a hard constraint, we'd rather not double TCO.
[00:46] Priya: okay that's helpful, in the console i'll show prompt set groups, then the regression alerts tied to those sets. we also have an a/b simulator to replay past traffic against two model+prompt configs so you can see delta in quality and token cost.
[01:05] Speaker 1: [overlap] can i interrupt, when you say "prompt set" is that per-UX flow or per-user cohort?
[01:10] Priya: good q, you can scope prompt sets to whatever dimension you want — flow, cohort, locale — the UI shows grouping and you can attach labels and evaluation metrics.
[01:20] Jordan: jumping into the live console — sharing screen — ok loading the "Eval Playground" (note: transcript may show "Eval Play ground" or "Red wood optimize" sometimes).
[02:05] Priya: here's our prompt set for the summary use case — you can see baseline examples, golden labels, and the auto-generated evaluation metrics like ROUGE, hallucination score, and a custom business metric (clarity score).
[03:12] Aisha: how do you define hallucination score? it looks different from our internal heuristics.
[03:18] Priya: we compute a combination of faithfulness checks and model confidence heuristics, but you can plug in your own eval function via the API or upload a python scorer. some customers map it to an internal label. transcription note: says "hallucination scrawl" here sometimes.
[04:05] Ben: can you show the regression alerts — like if something drifts after a model update?
[04:12] Priya: sure — you create an alert policy, choose the trigger (absolute regression or relative lift), select the prompt sets and the metric, set a sensitivity (low/med/high), and choose notification channels (Slack, email, webhook).
[05:30] Priya: for example here's an alert when clarity score dropped by 8% after a variant rollout. it shows affected prompt slices, example failures, and you can drill into sequences and the model outputs side-by-side.
[06:05] Clara: nice — can that also show token delta so we can see cost impact?
[06:12] Priya: yes there's token breakdown per variant and an estimated cost delta per million requests, we pull in your billing profile for accurate unit costs. note: cost is estimated for hosted pricing; dedicated pricing is handled via committed capacity config.
[07:00] Jordan: question on a/b simulator — is that a real time replay or synthetic?
[07:06] Priya: it replays historical requests you upload, or you can point to a live traffic capture for a dry-run. it runs them in sandboxed execution and gives you side-by-side metrics plus sample diffs. it can simulate batching and prefix cache behavior to estimate latency too.
[08:15] Ben: hmmm how accurate is the latency sim for our infra? we run on mixed GPUs and sometimes the kernel perf is different.
[08:22] Priya: good point — we provide hardware profiles and you can select the closest match; for Dedicated we will run an on-prem microbenchmark with your model artifact to get more precise numbers. ask: we're happy to run a short benchmark for you.
[09:05] Aisha: security — we need SOC2 type 2, SSO with SAML, audit logs that tie tokens to actions, and KMS integration, can we get those docs?
[09:15] Jordan: yes, we have SOC2, ISO docs; SSO via SAML/Okta, RBAC, audit log export, and KMS/HSM options for Private. we'll share the security pack after this call.
[09:40] Clara: what about data retention? we need 30 day rolling logs but some customers demand 90 days.
[09:49] Jordan: retention is configurable for enterprise tiers; we'll include retention levels in the doc.
[10:10] Priya: demo: now i'll show an A/B playback — running the simulator with two prompt variants and a smaller model vs larger: Variant A is our tuned prompt + quantized model, Variant B is looser prompt + full precision.
[12:30] Priya: results table — clarity: +6% for A, hallucination: -2% for A, cost per 1M tokens: A is $1,200, B is $2,700. latency median: A 540ms, B 420ms (because B uses a bigger model on better hw). so tradeoffs are visible; you can export the report as CSV or attach to a rollout policy.
[14:02] Ben: those deltas are huge — can we run this against our own logs?
[14:08] Priya: yes please upload a sample of your production logs (obfuscated) or we can ingest from your proxy. we also support streaming replays from a signed S3 URI.
[15:30] Aisha: okay for the POC we want three things: 1) run our replay against the two configs to validate quality/cost, 2) a canary rollout with automatic fallback if regressions exceed thresholds, 3) a security packet and pricing for dedicated capacity.
[15:50] Jordan: perfect — next steps on that — we'll provision a sandbox project, Priya will run the replay, and i'll follow up with pricing and the security docs.
[16:00] Priya: quick note: the canary policies allow metric gates, time windows, and a fallback model. the fallback can be to a cheaper quantized variant or to a regional mirror; we also support gradual traffic splits.
[17:20] Clara: how do you handle prefix caching for streaming summarization? we saw some regressions when KV cache warmed.
[17:28] Priya: we surface a cache-warmup simulator; in the replay you can enable KV cache emulation and see warm/cold latency curves. it also estimates per-token cache hits and the cost savings.
[18:45] Ben: what about integrations — we want a simple way to trigger retrain or label collection when alerts fire.
[18:52] Priya: alerts can call webhooks to kick workflows; customers often integrate with their labeling queue (Labelbox, internal). you can also attach a rule to create an eval task that pushes bad examples to a review board.
[20:05] Aisha: curious about false positives on alerts — we don't want noisy slack channels.
[20:12] Priya: you can set rolling windows, minimal sample sizes, and suppressions. also the UI suggests thresholds based on historical variance — call this "auto-suggest sensitivity".
[21:00] Jordan: there's also the Optimize suggestions — automated batching and quantization recs for a given workload. Priya can trigger Optimize to produce a cost/latency frontier.
[21:23] Priya: yep, Optimize will suggest batch sizes, preferred kernels, and a quantization profile and show estimated regressions per metric. we can also export a picklist for the infra team.
[22:40] Clara: what's the typical time to run a replay for 1 week of traffic?
[22:45] Priya: depends on size — we parallelize; a 100k-request sample usually finishes in a few hours in the sandbox; for the POC we can do a representative 10k sample and give quick results same day.
[24:00] Ben: network isolation — for private deployment do you provide a control plane reachable via private link?
[24:07] Jordan: yes for Private we deploy a control plane reachable via customer VPC endpoints, and on-prem packages are available for air-gapped setups.
[25:20] [long demo silence as Priya scrolls through the console, sample diffs displayed]
[28:15] Priya: showing the example diffs — you can see original prompt, both model replies, and a highlight of hallucinated spans. there's a diff viewer and a pairwise comparison mode. some transcribed labels may read as "pair-wise compare" or "pear-wise" in places.
[31:40] Aisha: will this tool support scheduled regressions scans? we want nightly scans across core prompt sets.
[31:48] Priya: yes you can schedule runs, and alerts can be tied to scheduled scans so you catch nightly regressions.
[34:10] Ben: licensing question — if we want dedicated capacity plus long term logs, is that a separate contract?
[34:18] Jordan: Dedicated is reserved capacity with an annual commitment; logging/retention and enterprise features are part of the enterprise package or add-ons, we'll outline pricing tiers.
[36:05] Clara: what about stakeholder reports for product and legal? can we export a compliance-ready packet?
[36:12] Priya: there are export templates for exec reports and audit packages that include examples, metric histories, and the security artifacts.
[38:30] [brief cross talk about timezone iCal invites and who will own the POC]
[40:00] Aisha: we'd like Priya to run a small replay and then a technical deep dive with your infra engineer to validate kernel perf. can we schedule that next week?
[40:08] Priya: yes i'm available wed/thurs next week, we can include our infra lead for the microbenchmark.
[42:20] Jordan: recap — deliverables: security docs, pricing for dedicated, sandbox project with replay run, technical deep dive + microbenchmark, and a short exec slide summarizing results.
[42:36] Aisha: sounds good, also can you include a recommended canary policy for our p95 goal?
[42:43] Priya: yes we'll suggest a policy and initial thresholds based on your historical variance.
[44:00] Ben: for the replay we'll prepare a 10k sample, scrubbed of PII, and share via signed S3 link.
[44:08] Aisha: we'll also add a product PM to the follow-up invite.
[46:10] Jordan: any competitor considerations? we can briefly note differences, but our focus is on end-to-end eval + rollout automation.
[46:18] Clara: we've looked at Anthropic and OpenAI endpoints and an in-house self-hosted runtime; primary motivators are predictable cost and easier rollouts.
[46:35] Priya: noted. also for the bench we can show both hosted and dedicated sim so you can compare.
[48:00] [wrap-up administrative chat about next meeting times and invites]
[50:11] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll send calendar invites and the security packet, Priya will run the replay and share the first report, i'll send pricing.
[50:20] Aisha: thanks, excited to see results.
[50:30] Meeting end — recording stopped

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcriptions and speaker label noise (Speaker 1/2), run-on sentences preserved.

Priya to provision sandbox project and run 10k replay against two configs (deliverable by 2025-11-10)

SummitTech to upload scrubbed 10k sample to signed S3 URI (by 2025-11-07)
